data: What is the approximate highest precision value recorded in graph (b)?

The question asks for the approximate highest precision value recorded in graph (b). From the caption, we know that the figure shows precision-biased results on the dev-set. The graph (b) is labeled as "Risk vs. Precision," which means it plots precision against risk threshold. 

Looking at the graph (b), we can see three lines representing different edge states: edge state, edge factored, and edge higher. These lines show a downward trend as the risk threshold increases. The highest point of each line corresponds to the maximum precision value for that particular edge state. 

By visually inspecting the graph, the highest precision value appears to be around 97%. This is the approximate value where the lines start their downward trend. Therefore, the approximate highest precision value recorded in graph (b) is 97%.
